mainTopic: The אונס versus the מפתה: forced marriage and the limits of עשה דוחה לא תעשה. The orphan who was engaged and divorced, and whose קנס is hers. How בושת, פגם and the fixed קנס are measured.
overview: The גמרא first finishes a point from the previous daf. Only the אונס is forced to marry the girl, because the פסוק about the מפתה says 'לו', meaning only if he wants. Next, רב כהנא asks why the אונס's מצוה to marry her does not override a prohibition when she is forbidden to him. רב זביד answers that an עשה only overrides a לא תעשה when it cannot be fulfilled any other way. Here she can refuse, and then the עשה disappears. A new משנה follows: רבי אלעזר rules that a man who rapes an orphan who was engaged and divorced pays the fine, while a seducer does not. רבי יוחנן shows that רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא: a girl who was engaged and divorced is like an orphan, so her קנס belongs to her. רב rules like רבי אלעזר. Then another משנה explains that בושת and פגם depend on the people involved, but the קנס is the same for everyone. The גמרא asks whether the fifty סלעים might cover everything. רבי זירא answers with an argument from fairness, and אביי begins to challenge it from the fixed price of a slave, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not learn forced marriage from each other too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the אונס and the מפתה are not compared for the rule of forced marriage as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: For this matter too, let them be learned from each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the difference between the two cases. The אונס must marry her even against his will, so the מפתה should also be forced to marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא said the אונס and the מפתה are learned from each other in many details. So why not in this detail too? If they were compared, the מפתה would also be forced to marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who forced himself on a girl (a rapist)
A man who seduced a girl, who agreed to it
Let them be learned from each other

phrases.english: For this matter too
phrases.notes: 'This matter' is marrying her even when the man does not want to.

phrases.english: let them be learned from each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous daf comparing the אונס and the מפתה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between the אונס, who is forced to marry, and the מפתה, who is not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two cases are learned from each other in other details, the same comparison should apply to forced marriage.

steps.title: The word 'לו' means only with his consent
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about the מפתה says 'לו', which teaches that he marries her only if he wants to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'He shall surely pay a dowry for her to be a wife to him.' 'To him' means with his consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a word in the פסוק. The word 'לו' shows that the מפתה only marries her if he agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clear word in the פסוק is stronger than the general comparison between the two cases. So for this one detail, the מפתה is different from the אונס. The אונס still 'drinks from his vessel' and must marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: With his consent / by his own will

steps.whatToRemember: The מפתה only marries her if he wants to ('לו', with his consent). The אונס must marry her even against his will.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'He shall surely pay a dowry for her to be a wife to him,'
'to him' means with his consent.

steps.terutzResolutionType: A special word in the פסוק excludes this detail from the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the two cases are learned from each other, the מפתה should also be forced to marry her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'לו' shows that the מפתה marries her only if he agrees.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: how does he 'drink from his vessel'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'כיצד שותה בעציצו' to start a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'How does he drink from his vessel?' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה to begin a new topic. This line sets up the question that רב כהנא is about to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that the אונס must marry her even if she has a blemish. But if she is forbidden to him, he may not marry her. The next step will challenge that second part.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Drinks from his vessel', meaning he must marry her and stay with her
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quote is in the משנה

phrases.english: 'How does he drink from his vessel?' etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of that משנה. If she is forbidden to him, he does not marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אונס must marry her, unless she is forbidden to him.

steps.title: Why doesn't the מצוה to marry her override the prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asked רב זביד why the עשה of marrying her does not push aside the לא תעשה that forbids her to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I said this teaching before רב זביד of נהרדעא: Let the positive מצוה come and push aside the prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges the משנה's rule that the אונס does not marry a woman who is forbidden to him. The general rule is that an עשה pushes aside a לא תעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אונס has an עשה: 'ולו תהיה לאשה' (she shall be his wife). When an עשה clashes with a לא תעשה, the עשה usually wins. So he should be allowed, and even required, to marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה (a 'do' command)
A prohibition (a 'do not' command)
The rule that a positive מצוה overrides a prohibition
A teaching or halachic ruling

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
I said this teaching
before Rav Zevid of Neharde'a:
Let the positive מצוה come
phrases.notes: The positive מצוה is 'and she shall be his wife' (דברים 22:29).

phrases.english: and push aside the prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the אונס does not marry a woman who is forbidden to him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Normally an עשה overrides a לא תעשה, so the מצוה to marry her should override the prohibition.

steps.title: The מצוה only overrides when it cannot be avoided
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains that עשה דוחה לא תעשה applies only when the עשה cannot be done any other way, like מילה on skin with צרעת. Here she can refuse, which cancels the עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Where do we say a positive מצוה comes and pushes aside a prohibition? In a case like מילה on skin with צרעת, where there is no way to fulfill the positive מצוה otherwise. But here, if she says 'I don't want him,' is there a positive מצוה at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers that the rule of עשה דוחה לא תעשה does not apply here. The עשה of marrying her is not fixed, because she can refuse and cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מילה בצרעת, you cannot do the מילה without cutting the צרעת, so the עשה wins. Here, the woman can simply say she does not want him, and then the עשה is gone. An עשה that can be avoided this way does not override a לא תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Circumcision on skin that has צרעת, which may not normally be cut off
To fulfill it
I don't want (him)

steps.whatToRemember: עשה דוחה לא תעשה works only when the עשה cannot be fulfilled any other way. The מצוה of the אונס to marry her depends on her consent, so it does not override a prohibition.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the אונס has no מצוה at all. The מצוה exists, but she can cancel it by refusing. Because of that, it is not strong enough to push aside a לא תעשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important limit on the principle of עשה דוחה לא תעשה, and that limit appears in many places in the גמרא.

phrases.english: He said to me:
Where do we say
that a positive מצוה comes and pushes aside a prohibition
For example, מילה on skin with צרעת,
phrases.notes: Cutting off צרעת is forbidden, but the ברית requires cutting it, so the ברית wins.

phrases.english: where it is not possible to fulfill the positive מצוה otherwise.
But here,
if she says, 'I don't want him,'
is there a positive מצוה at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא אָמְרִינַן נֵיתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְנִידְחֵי לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the principle עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every עשה overrides a לא תעשה, so the אונס should marry her even if she is forbidden to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an עשה that cannot be fulfilled any other way overrides a לא תעשה. The אונס's מצוה can be cancelled by her refusal.

steps.title: New משנה: the orphan who was engaged and divorced
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a man who rapes an orphan who was engaged and divorced must pay, but a man who seduces her does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An orphan who was engaged and then divorced. רבי אלעזר says: the one who rapes her is obligated, and the one who seduces her is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי אלעזר says that in the case of this girl, the אונס pays the fine but the מפתה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This girl is still a virgin, so the אונס must pay the fine. The fine for seduction belongs to her, and she agreed to the seduction, so the מפתה is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphan girl (her father has died)
Was engaged, through the first stage of marriage (אירוסין)
Obligated / exempt

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An orphan who was engaged and then divorced,
Rabbi Elazar says:
The one who rapes her is obligated,
and the one who seduces her is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an orphan who was engaged and divorced, the אונס pays the fine and the מפתה is exempt.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר follows his teacher רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that רבי אלעזר's ruling follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that a girl who was engaged and divorced gets a קנס, and the קנס goes to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי אלעזר's ruling follows his teacher רבי עקיבא, who said that such a girl gets a fine, and the fine goes to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by linking רבי אלעזר's ruling from the משנה to an earlier opinion of רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי עקיבא said that a נערה who was engaged and then divorced still gets a קנס if she is raped, and the money goes to her, not to her father. רבי יוחנן says רבי אלעזר holds the same way. The next step will show how we know this.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed fine the Torah sets for a rapist or seducer
To herself, meaning the money belongs to the girl and not to her father
Following the view of

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רַבּוֹ אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said it following the view of Rabbi Akiva, his teacher,
who said: she has a fine
phrases.notes: This is about the girl from an earlier משנה who was engaged and then divorced.

phrases.english: and her fine goes to herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains whose view רבי אלעזר's ruling from the משנה (step 6) is based on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר follows רבי עקיבא: a girl who was engaged and divorced gets a קנס, and it goes to her.

steps.title: The proof from the orphan ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the link from רבי אלעזר's words about an orphan: the rapist pays and the seducer does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know? Because the משנה teaches about an orphan: רבי אלעזר says the rapist must pay and the seducer is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי עקיבא, and points back to his ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is quoted again here on purpose, as evidence. The seducer is exempt because the money would go to the girl herself, and she agreed. That only makes sense if the קנס belongs to her. Step 9 asks why the orphan case needed to be taught at all, and step 10's answer shows how it proves something about a divorced girl.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
From the fact that it teaches
An orphan girl with no father
One who rapes / one who seduces

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From the fact that it teaches: an orphan,
Rabbi Elazar says:
the one who rapes is obligated, and the one who seduces is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's ruling in the משנה about the יתומה.

steps.title: Why mention an orphan? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר needed to teach the orphan case, since its result seems obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר bothered to say something so obvious. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An orphan has no father, so the קנס clearly belongs to her. If she agreed to the seduction, of course the seducer pays nothing. So the ruling must be teaching something more.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: An orphan? That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the proof text from step 8, which seems to say something obvious.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea is the orphan ruling teaching?

steps.title: A divorced girl is treated like an orphan
steps.stepSummary: The ruling teaches that a girl who was engaged and divorced is like an orphan: her קנס goes to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches us that a girl who was engaged and divorced is like an orphan. Just as an orphan's fine goes to her, so too this girl's fine goes to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'orphan' is a comparison. It teaches us how to treat a girl who was engaged and divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if her father is alive, a girl who was engaged and divorced is treated like an orphan for the קנס, so the money is hers. This is exactly רבי עקיבא's view, which completes the proof from step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the new thing it teaches us
Was engaged (אירוסין) and then divorced

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, who follows רבי עקיבא, a נערה who was engaged and divorced is like an orphan: the קנס is hers. That is why a seducer she agreed to is exempt.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches us:
that a young woman who was engaged and divorced is like an orphan.
Just as with an orphan, the fine goes to herself,
so too with a young woman who was engaged and divorced, the fine goes to herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 and finishes the proof of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The orphan case teaches that a girl who was engaged and divorced has the same status as an orphan, so her קנס goes to her.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Through a long chain of teachers, רב rules like רבי אלעזר and calls him the happiest of the Sages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבה בר שילא, in the name of רב המנונא סבא, in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה, in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר. רב called רבי אלעזר 'the happiest of the Sages.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: we follow רבי אלעזר. It adds רב's praise of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long chain of names shows how the ruling was handed down from teacher to student. רב's nickname for רבי אלעזר shows his high regard for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows (this person)
The Elder
The happiest (most fortunate) of the Sages

steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, a rapist of an orphan or of a girl who was engaged and divorced pays the קנס, and a seducer does not.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabba bar Sheila said
that Rav Hamnuna the Elder said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Elazar.
Rav would call Rabbi Elazar:
"the happiest of the Sages."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final halacha on רבי אלעזר's ruling that was just explained.

steps.title: New משנה: how shame, lowered value, and the fine are measured
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that בושת depends on the people involved, פגם is measured like a maidservant's market value, and the קנס is the same for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the payment for shame? It all depends on who caused the shame and who was shamed. Lowered value: we look at her as if she were a maidservant sold in the market, and see how much she was worth before and how much she is worth now. The fine is the same for everyone, and anything with a fixed amount from the Torah is the same for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains how to measure three of the payments a rapist or seducer may owe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בושת changes from case to case, based on the status of both people. פגם is the drop in her value, measured by imagining her sold as a maidservant. The קנס never changes, because the Torah set a fixed amount, and any Torah-fixed payment is the same for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Payment for shame or embarrassment
Payment for her lowered value
A maidservant
A fixed, set amount

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three payments: בושת and פגם change from case to case, but the קנס is always the same amount.

phrases.english: MISHNA
What is the payment for shame?
It all depends on the one who shames and the one who is shamed.
Lowered value:
we look at her as if she were
a maidservant being sold in the market,

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה הָיְתָה יָפָה, וְכַמָּה הִיא יָפָה.
phrases.english: how much she was worth before, and how much she is worth now.
phrases.notes: Literally 'how pretty,' but here it means how much money she is worth.

phrases.english: The fine is the same for every person,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קִצְבָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: and anything that has a fixed amount from the Torah
phrases.notes: The Torah sets the קנס at fifty silver pieces (דברים 22:29).

phrases.english: is the same for every person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on how each payment is measured.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בושת depends on both people; פגם is measured by her value as a maidservant before and after; the קנס and every Torah-fixed payment is the same for everyone.

steps.title: Why not say the fifty סלעים cover everything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah's fifty סלעים should not be the whole payment, covering shame and damage as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why not say the Torah's fifty סלעים are the payment for all the losses together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It asks whether the fifty סלעים the Torah mentions might be one all-inclusive payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the אונס pays בושת and פגם on top of the קנס. The פסוק only mentions fifty silver pieces. So the גמרא suggests the fifty might cover everything, which would leave no room for extra payments.

keyTerms.meaning: And let me say; a way of suggesting a different reading
Silver coins; the Torah's fine is fifty of them
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the Torah
For all matters; one payment covering everything

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But say: the Merciful One said fifty סלעים,
phrases.notes: This refers to the fifty silver pieces in דברים 22:29.

phrases.english: for all the matters!
phrases.notes: He means the fine, the shame and the damage all together, with nothing paid beyond the fifty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: חֲמִשִּׁים סְלָעִים אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, מִכֹּל מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה from step 12, which listed בושת and פגם as payments on top of the קנס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that בושת and פגם are paid in addition to the fixed קנס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק mentions only fifty סלעים, so maybe that sum covers every loss.

steps.title: A princess and a commoner cannot get the same amount
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that a single flat sum would be unfair, since people would complain that a king's daughter and a commoner's daughter receive equal payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: People would say, 'If he violated a king's daughter, fifty; if he violated a commoner's daughter, also fifty?!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains why the fifty cannot cover everything: it would treat very different girls the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shame and damage differ from person to person, as step 12 said. If one fixed sum covered everything, a princess's huge loss and a commoner's smaller loss would be paid equally, which seems unjust. So the fifty is only the קנס, and the other payments change with the case.

keyTerms.meaning: They will say; people would complain
He had relations with (here, by force)
A daughter of kings; a princess
Commoners; ordinary people

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: They will say:
If he violated a daughter of kings, fifty;
if he violated a daughter of commoners, also fifty?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13's suggestion and defends the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifty סלעים might cover every loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: A flat sum would pay a princess and a commoner equally, which is unfair, so בושת and פגם must be paid separately.

steps.title: But the Torah does fix one price for a slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבי זירא: the Torah sets a flat thirty for a slave killed by an ox, even though slaves differ greatly in value.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, people would say about a slave too: a slave who drills pearls, thirty; a slave who does…
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבי זירא's argument. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said a fixed sum would be unfair. אביי points out that the Torah does exactly that for a slave killed by an ox: always thirty, whether the slave was highly skilled or not. So 'people will complain' cannot by itself prove that the fifty is not all-inclusive.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introducing a problem that follows from the last statement
A slave (here a Canaanite slave)
Drills holes in pearls; a valuable, skilled job

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the slave payment is unfair. He means the Torah clearly does set flat amounts sometimes, so רבי זירא's fairness argument is not decisive.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: If so,
regarding a slave as well, they will say:
phrases.notes: This is the slave killed by an ox, where the owner pays thirty silver pieces (שמות 21:32).

phrases.english: a slave who drills pearls, thirty,
a slave who does

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's answer in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's argument that a fixed sum for everyone would be unacceptable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah fixes thirty for any slave killed by an ox, skilled or not, so a flat sum regardless of value is possible.
